skepticism_findings: Filters are vendor-domain/host rules, not corpus strings verbatim: probes with novel paths/subdomains (newads.criteo.net, cdn-77.hotstar.com/ads/x.mp4) block, and content URLs (aiv-cdn.amazon.com/video/, hotstar subtitles .vtt) do not. Stitched items (5) and unlisted hosts are correctly unblocked and counted in the denominator.
Circularity remains: corpus hosts are mostly from the same vendor lists as the rules (confidence vendor-known 53/59 PV, 38/43 JH), so rates are expected to be high. Real-world rate is unmeasured.

3 AT-8 false positives are real: https://www.iab.com/guidelines/vast/, https://blog.example.com/what-is-vpaid, https://docs.example.org/vast/overview are blocked by VAST/VPAID heuristics (DNR/path token). 0.21% is under the <2% limit, but the author seeded only 4 such edge URLs (1 is correctly passed), so the real FP rate on VAST-related pages could be higher. These are main-frame-like page URLs; confirm DNR does not block main_frame navigations.
Clean corpus: only ~350 of 1414 URLs are real domains (rest synthetic/lookalike), so 0.21% flatters the real rate.
Content script overhead measures scan time on jsdom, not page load delta; margin is thin and flaky (see performance).
blockers: jsdom is not in devDependencies (package-lock.json is root-owned); the benchmark relies on the transitive copy via jest-environment-jsdom. A human must run: npm install --save-dev jsdom
Corpora unconfirmed; manual items unrun, so the SPEC Definition of Done cannot be declared met
